Cognate with Icelandic lækur and Faroese løkur (“brook, stream”); more distantly related to Welsh llaith (“wet, moist”), Armenian լիճ (lič, “lake”) and English leak. / Origin uncertain.

a female given name from Latin [in turn from Ancient Greek], equivalent to English Alexandra, the feminine form of Alexander

1000311.etyen:
The feminine counterpart of Alexander. Derived from Latin Alexandra (“female given name”), from Ancient Greek Ἀλεξάνδρα (Alexándra), the feminine form of Ἀλέξανδρος (Aléxandros, “male given name”). The name is traditionally analysed as ἀλέξω (aléxō, “to ward off, defend”) and ἀνήρ (anḗr, “man”), genitive ἀνδρός (andrós), hence “defender of men” or “protector of men”.
Compare Danish Alexandra, Swedish Alexandra, Icelandic Alexandra, English Alexandra and German Alexandra (“female given name”).

1004663.etyen: A regional form of ringakake, from ring (“ring”) + kake (“cake, baked good”), with linking -a- (“interfix”). The vowel e in the first element reflects the lowering of i to e found in the traditional dialect of Rana. The name refers to the concentric rings or spiral in which the dough is arranged.
